newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside to cut Cossack output Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside to cut Cossack output Oct 15.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd plans to commence maintenance and repair work at the offshore Cossack Pioneer crude oil facility on October 15, which will reduce daily output to 50,000-60,000 barrels a day from around 115,000 currently, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The work is expected take between two and three weeks to complete, he said.
"It will reduce oil production probably to between 50,000 and 60,000 barrels a day," the spokesman said.
The work is being undertaken to repair the facility's gas export system, the spokesman said.
"Because of the problems to the gas export system, they've had the need to shut it down to do some work to it," he said.

Cossack Pioneer, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wannea and Cossack fields in the North West Shelf, has been plagued by weather-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year.
"We'll be down to about 50 percent capacity basically," the spokesman said.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are Woodside, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd and units of Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, British Petrolem Co Plc, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group
